subject: Post-call: Prompt set collection & redaction guidance for model fit / evals
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Prompt set collection & redaction guidance for model fit / evals

Hi Tara —

Great to meet with you earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the model-fit evals moving: 

1) We’ll collect a representative prompt set from your team (happy path + edge cases + redaction examples). I’ve attached a prompt_collection_template.csv you can fill out — one prompt per row, with columns for expected intent, redaction hints, and a flag for PII-sensitive content.

2) Recommended starting models for your use case (customer support summarization + policy-aware responses):
   - redwood-llm-2-7b (quantized) — very cost-effective for high throughput; strong summarization on 2–4k context.
   - redwood-llm-13b (fp16) — if you need higher factuality and instruction-following on tricky legal text.

3) We’ll run benchmark evals using your prompts and our standard regressions suite; we’ll share per-prompt quality scores and latency/cost tradeoffs. Example report (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-benchmark-reports

4) Redaction guidance: please flag any prompts with PII in the template and include an anonymized version where possible. We also included a short redaction_guidance.pdf with recommended patterns (emails, SSNs, account IDs). If you prefer, we can accept a redacted and an original version over a secure link and redact on our side before storing.

Next steps: could you and Sam (if helpful) drop 20–50 representative prompts into the attached template by next Tuesday (2026-09-08)? Once we have that, Logan (SE) will run the evals and we’ll follow up with model recommendations and a quality/latency report.

Thanks — excited to get started.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Attachments: prompt_collection_template.csv, redaction_guidance.pdf

From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 18:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Prompt set collection & redaction guidance for model fit / evals

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. Sam and I started pulling examples. A few quick clarifications: 

- We have a mix of support transcripts and internal policy text that will be sensitive. We can anonymize the transcripts but need guidance on which fields to remove vs keep for context (e.g., timestamps, order numbers).
- For edge cases: we’ll include disputes/escalations, refund policy conflicts, and some multi-turn escalation flows.

I attached a starter CSV (acme_prompt_samples.csv) with ~10 prompts. We’ll aim to get to 30 by Tuesday. Can you confirm: do you want the redacted AND original versions? Also cc’ing our security contact (Sam) — he may have constraints on how we upload originals.

Appreciate it,
Tara
Tara Singh | Senior Product Manager, CX
Acme Retail
tara.singh@acme.com | (212) 555-4982
Attachments: acme_prompt_samples.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Prompt set collection & redaction guidance for model fit / evals

Internal — forwarding Tara’s starter set and the ask. Key points:

- Acme will drop ~30 prompts (mix of support transcripts, policy text, escalation flows). They can provide redacted+original if we give secure upload.
- Suggested initial model sweep: redwood-llm-2-7b (quant) and redwood-llm-13b (fp16). Need to confirm throughput/latency targets vs cost.
- Please run our standard prompt-level regressions + the safety/redaction check. Capture per-prompt quality (ROUGE/ROUGE-L + human score), latency p95, and token cost.
Can you take point, Logan? If you want me to schedule a quick 30-min sync with Tara/Sam next week, I can coordinate.

Deal: ACME-2026-042 (HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-042)
—Marissa

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Prompt set collection & redaction guidance for model fit / evals

Thanks Marissa — I’ll take this on. Plan:

1) Ingest the 30 prompts into our eval harness (will keep originals in a secure bucket flagged for SRE-only access).
2) Run model sweep: redwood-llm-2-7b-quant, redwood-llm-13b-fp16, and a smaller check against a 3rd-party baseline (for reference).
3) Output: per-prompt quality table (automated metrics + short human spot-check notes), latency p50/p95, and estimated per-token cost. I’ll attach the draft report to the HubSpot deal once finished.
Questions:
- Target latency SLO for customer-facing flows? (Marissa / Tara suggested sub-600ms p95 for single-turn summarization.)
- For redaction: do we require originals to be retained for debugging post-deployment, or should we only keep redacted versions? If originals are retained, Acme will need an export agreement signed.
I’ll start the runs Monday and aim to share a first-pass report by Wednesday EOD PT.

—Logan
